notes.text: Jordan Staal is out 1-2 months (calf tear) and has missed the last 13 games. Mark Jankowski has taken his spot beside Jordan Martinook and Nikolaj Ehlers.
Jared McCann is out 10 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Matthew Wood joined from NSH on Nov 2 and has played beside Chandler Stephenson and Frédérick Gaudreau.
Vince Dunn has started killing penalties: on the ice for 41% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, up from 2% last season.

stakes: The Hurricanes go in first in the Metropolitan with 30 points, the Kraken fourth in the Pacific with 19 points.

SEA.head: The Kraken have their work cut out
SEA.body: Even though Seattle has home-ice advantage and gets Fleury back, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Seattle will be without McCann. The Kraken can still win it if they keep dangerous shots away, but a lot has to go their way.

story.head: The Hurricanes are going to let it fly
paras: The Kraken (9-6-1) lost 4-3 to the Rangers on Saturday. The Hurricanes have won two in a row, the last a 9-2 rout of Chicago. Going in, the Hurricanes are first in the Metropolitan (tied for second in the NHL) and the Kraken fourth in the Pacific (tied for 18th).
The Hurricanes’ record (.789) is about what their chances are worth. The Kraken’s record (.594) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.449), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd). The Kraken, by contrast, rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd). Carolina has scored 4.11 goals a game, the most in the league, and allowed 2.32, the fourth fewest. On the other side, the Kraken have a leaky penalty kill (31st). They also give up a lot of shots (32nd), so the Canes are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against them. Both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Sebastian Aho (10 G / 16 A / 26 P in 19 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for ninth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Logan Stankoven (11 G / 7 A / 18 P in 19 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. For the Kraken, Berkly Catton (5 G / 9 A / 14 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Frédérick Gaudreau (7 G / 3 A / 10 P in 16 GP) has a team-high seven goals.

Pyotr Kochetkov (11-1-0 / .920 SV% in 12 GS) has been terrific for Carolina and will likely start. Seattle has two options in net: Philipp Grubauer (5-3-1 / .890 SV% in 8 GS) and Joey Daccord (4-3-0 / .881 SV% in 8 GS). Grubauer has started six of their last ten games, but Daccord got the last one on Saturday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

At home, Lane Lambert likes to send Nyman, Meyers and Winterton out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Robinson, Kotkaniemi and Martinook. One more thing: the Hurricanes usually control more of the chances than the Kraken do.

items.text: Taylor Hall is set to play his 1,000th NHL game.
The Hurricanes have been without Jordan Staal since Oct 10.
The Kraken are newly without Cale Fleury, and have been without Jared McCann since Oct 22.
Mackie Samoskevich has six goals on chances worth about 2.5 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
